hook: Eliezer Yudkowsky is an American writer and researcher who has spent more than two decades arguing that artificial intelligence poses a serious risk to humanity's survival. Without a formal academic degree, he co-founded the Singularity Institute for Artificial Intelligence, later renamed the Machine Intelligence Research Institute, with Brian and Sabine Atkins in 2000 to help accelerate the arrival of smarter than human AI. Within a few years he concluded that building such systems safely was a harder and more urgent problem than building them at all, and he redirected the institute's research toward what became known as AI alignment. Between 2006 and 2012 he wrote a long series of essays on rationality, cognitive bias, and AI risk that helped found the online community LessWrong and were later collected into the book Rationality: From AI to Zombies. In 2023 he argued in a Time magazine essay that a temporary pause on AI development was not enough and called for governments to shut down large AI training runs entirely. In 2025 he co-authored If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies with fellow MIRI researcher Nate Soares, bringing his warnings about superintelligent AI to a mainstream audience.
name: Eliezer Yudkowsky

quote.text: If somebody builds a too-powerful AI, under present conditions, I expect that every single member of the human species and all biological life on Earth dies shortly thereafter.
quote.context: From his Time magazine essay, Pausing AI Developments Isn't Enough. We Need to Shut It All Down, March 29, 2023

timeline.event: Co-founded the Singularity Institute for Artificial Intelligence, later renamed the Machine Intelligence Research Institute, with Brian and Sabine Atkins.
timeline.impact: Created one of the first organizations dedicated full time to AI safety research.

timeline.event: Concluded that aligning smarter than human AI with human values was a harder problem than building the AI itself, and redirected the institute's research accordingly.
timeline.impact: Set the research agenda that later became known as AI alignment.

timeline.event: Published Artificial Intelligence as a Positive and Negative Factor in Global Risk in the Oxford University Press volume Global Catastrophic Risks.
timeline.impact: Gave AI existential risk arguments an early academic platform.

timeline.event: Concluded a multi-year series of essays on rationality, cognitive bias, and AI risk written on Overcoming Bias and LessWrong since 2006.
timeline.impact: Built an online community that became a hub for rationality and AI safety discussion.

timeline.event: Collected his rationality essays into the book Rationality: From AI to Zombies.
timeline.impact: Made his framework for reasoning about bias and AI risk available to a much wider readership.

timeline.event: Published the Time magazine essay Pausing AI Developments Isn't Enough. We Need to Shut It All Down.
timeline.impact: Pushed the argument for halting frontier AI development into mainstream media debate.

timeline.event: Co-authored the book If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies with Nate Soares.
timeline.impact: Brought his case for the danger of superintelligent AI to a general audience in book form.
